what_its_for: Anakinra is used to treat rheumatoid arthritis (RA) in adults when other medicines have not worked well enough. It is also used to treat a rare but serious condition called Neonatal-Onset Multisystem Inflammatory Disease (NOMID) and certain other inflammatory conditions. It works by blocking a protein in your body called interleukin-1 (IL-1), which causes inflammation and joint damage.
how_to_take: Anakinra comes as a liquid in a pre-filled syringe and is given as an injection under your skin (subcutaneous injection), similar to how insulin is injected. Common injection sites include your stomach area (abdomen), thighs, or upper arms. Rotate your injection sites each time so you do not use the same spot twice in a row. Clean the skin with an alcohol wipe before injecting. Do not inject into skin that is bruised, red, tender, or hard. Your doctor or nurse will show you how to inject yourself properly before you do it on your own.
dosing: For rheumatoid arthritis in adults, the usual dose is 100 mg injected once every day at about the same time each day. For NOMID, the dose is based on your body weight and will be determined by your doctor. Always follow the exact dose your doctor prescribes — do not change your dose without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, inject it as soon as you remember on the same day. If you do not remember until the next day, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do not inject two doses in one day to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store anakinra in the refrigerator at 36°F to 46°F (2°C to 8°C). Do not freeze it — if the syringe has been frozen, throw it away and use a new one. Keep it away from light. You may take it out of the refrigerator and keep it at room temperature (up to 77°F/25°C) for up to 24 hours, but do not put it back in the refrigerator after it has been kept at room temperature. Keep it in the original carton until you are ready to use it. Keep out of reach of children. Do not use syringes that are expired, discolored, cloudy, or contain visible particles.
what_to_avoid: Do not use anakinra if you have an active infection — tell your doctor right away if you feel sick or have signs of infection. Avoid receiving live vaccines (such as MMR, chickenpox, or nasal flu vaccine) while using anakinra, as this can cause serious infections. Avoid using anakinra together with other biologic medicines like etanercept, adalimumab, or TNF blockers, as the combination greatly increases your risk of serious infections. Avoid touching the needle guard spring to prevent accidental injury.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you notice: signs of a serious infection such as fever, chills, cough, shortness of breath, burning when urinating, or a wound that will not heal; redness, swelling, pain, or bruising at the injection site that does not go away or gets worse; signs of an allergic reaction such as hives, rash, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing; unusual tiredness, pale skin, or feeling faint (possible low blood cell counts); or any new or worsening symptoms that concern you.
when_it_works: Some people notice improvement in joint pain and swelling within a few weeks, but it may take up to 3 months to feel the full benefit of the medicine. Keep taking it as directed even if you do not feel better right away. Do not stop without talking to your doctor first.
special_populations: Kidney problems: If you have severe kidney disease, your doctor may recommend injecting anakinra every other day instead of daily, since the medicine stays in your body longer. Older adults: Older patients may be more likely to get infections, so your doctor will watch you more closely. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. The effects of anakinra on unborn babies and nursing infants are not fully known, so always discuss the risks and benefits with your doctor. Children: Anakinra is approved for use in children with NOMID; dosing will be calculated by your doctor based on the child's weight.
